$comment: 🪟️ An action declared by a window body belongs to THAT window instance. The shell resolves `ActionAddress::window_instance_id` from the action's own `windowId` argument first, and only then falls back to the focused window — so an action that carries no `windowId` is addressed to whatever happens to be focused, and the guest refuses it when that window's KIND does not own the action. Measured on 6118: pressing the Generations window's `Add Generation` row produced `handle_action promise failed: window kind procedural-main does not own action addGeneration`. Context menus already scoped their actions this way; retained window bodies did not. One rule, one owner.

rule.statement: Scoping replaces any existing `windowId` argument with the owning window instance id, preserves every other argument in order, and creates the argument object when the action carried none.

cases.name: an-action-with-no-arguments-gains-the-window
cases.why: The live defect: the retained `Add Generation` row's action carries no arguments at all, so it resolved to the focused window `procedural-main`.

cases.name: existing-arguments-are-preserved-in-order
cases.why: Scoping must not disturb the payload the body authored.

cases.name: a-stale-window-id-is-replaced-not-duplicated
cases.why: A body re-scoped for another window must not leave two `windowId` entries for the address resolver to pick between.

cases.name: an-action-already-scoped-to-its-own-window-is-unchanged-in-meaning
cases.why: Idempotence — scoping twice addresses the same instance.
